keyFindings.description: The retention-gap fix still repeats the notice when the sweep is cut short. notify(retention_gap) runs at 734-741, before the page's frames are handled (762-775, each awaiting host.deliver and a flush per shown frame), and the moved cursor is written only at 787; a kill, a shutdown or a session switch (alive() false at 768/777 returns without the write) in between leaves the notice recorded held and the cursor below first_seq - 1, so after the resume the requeued notice and the re-found gap tell it twice. Both thermonuclear agents reproduced it with throwaway engine tests (notices: ['retention_gap','retention_gap']). The PR's SIGKILL test passes only because its expired messages are on an unfollowed subject. Fix: when the gap is found, lift the gapped subject's cursor to max(after, first_seq - 1), await flush(alive, true), then notify; that skips nothing and lets the atOnce plumbing go. Add an engine test that cuts the sweep while a frame of the gapped page is delivered.

restoreLocalSessionState calls requeueNotices (903) before releaseOtherSessions (916), and requeueNotices skips an id already held for any session; on a fork that copies the held notice's entry, the new session's requeue is skipped and the old session's copy is then dropped, so the forked session is not shown the notice until a restart. Release first, or dedupe on (sessionID, id).

'The hub's listener' (201-208) lists what a credential-less caller of port 9020 gets (publish, claim a role, list and delete sessions) and omits reading any session's stored inbox for 72 hours by id, which this PR adds.

Not proven / risk line 16 says those tailnet peers 'can already read live traffic through the hub's no-auth NATS user'; gcp/natshub.go sets NoAuthUser only when sessionUser is configured. Make it conditional.
